description: Labeled Agent reasoning excerpts and Codex status titles for the thought summarizer's housekeeping check (ADR 0036). `expected` is `skip` when the input is only the Agent's own process — reading its memory, notes, manual, instructions, or skills; checking its inbox or messages; claiming or updating tasks; deciding whether to reply; reading prior conversation just to orient — and `show` when it describes work on the person's request, including mixed inputs that mention housekeeping alongside that work.

cases.text: I'm going to read my memory first. Let me open MEMORY.md and see what I've recorded about this workspace before doing anything else.
Before I respond, I should check my MEMORY.md index and the notes files it points to so I have my standing context loaded.
There's a new request in #product. I'm looking to claim a task for it so nobody else picks it up. Let me run haus task claim on that message.
Let me check the task board to see which tasks are assigned to me and whether any are still open from yesterday.
The work is finished, so I need to update the task status to done and make sure the assignee is still me.
I got an inbox notice with three new items. Let me run haus message check to read what's pending before I decide anything.
This message is an FYI from Zach about the offsite. I'm deciding whether to reply at all — it doesn't seem to ask anything of me, so staying silent is probably right.
I don't remember the exact flags for scheduling a reminder. Let me search the Haus manual for the reminder-cron recipe and read it.
Before emitting any visual fence I'm supposed to read the visuals skill. Let me load that skill file first so I follow the fence contract.
Let me re-read my instructions about threads to make sure I'm sending to the right target and following the placement rules.
I was mentioned in a thread I haven't seen. Let me read the earlier messages in the thread to get oriented before anything else.
Let me confirm who I am here with haus profile show and check which channels I've joined so I know my identity and handle.

The chart is rendering with the wrong axis because the dates come back as strings. I need to parse them before building the series, then rerun the chart.
The staging deploy failed on the migration step. Let me look at the CI log for the failing job and see whether the new column conflicts with the old default.
Looking at the Halloween campaign bids: spend is up 40% but conversions are flat, so the long-tail keywords are probably overbidding. I'll list the worst ten.
Maya asked for a reply to the supplier about the late shipment. I'll draft something firm but polite that asks for a new ship date and tracking.
The worker's memory usage climbs every hour, which smells like a leak in the image cache. Let me profile the heap after a few hundred renders.
Tiny asked for release notes for v0.4. Let me go through the merged pull requests since the last tag and group them into fixes and features.
The Etsy title is too long for the ribbon shirt. I'll lead with the design name, then the product type, and drop the duplicate keyword at the end.

Reading memory for Zach's chart preference, then pulling sales. He likes weekly bars rather than lines, so once I have the numbers I'll build a bar chart of last month by week.
I'll claim this one quickly and then get into the bug itself: the checkout total double-counts tax when a coupon is applied, so the discount has to be subtracted before tax.
Skimming the thread to see what Priya already tried — she restarted the queue worker, so the stuck jobs must be a lock problem. Let me query for jobs holding a lease past expiry.
Zach wants a reminder to check the Amazon ad budget every Monday. I checked the manual for the flags; now scheduling the weekly budget check on his message.
My notes say the invoice template lives in the finance folder. Opening it now to fill in September's hours for the Acme invoice Maya asked for.
